key_insight: Mutual friction rolls quantized vortices into coherent bundles inside normal-fluid vortex tubes, linking superfluid organization to the spatial hierarchy of classical turbulence.
engineering_relevance: The findings could inform multiscale models of cryogenic helium flows by connecting vortex organization and thermal stability to two-fluid coupling timescales.
method: Fully coupled, two-way vortex filament and Navier–Stokes simulations.
Spatially periodic normal-fluid turbulence coupled to superfluid helium-4.
Analysis of vortex structures, energy spectra, and bundle lifetimes.
evidence_signal: Simulations show nested vortex structures and a Kolmogorov k^(-5/3) spectrum, with bundle lifetimes governed by the local coupling-to-dissipation timescale ratio t_cl/τ_η < 20.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation evidence in a spatially periodic setting; applicability to wall-bounded flows and experimental conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Two-Way Coupled Dynamics of Quantized Vortex Bundle Formation in Spatially Periodic Normal-Fluid Turbulence
